dedupeKey: quality|Exec/RunCommand argv loses its nax-config refusal with no write-refusal backstop|nax-agent/src/tools/package-managers.ts

action.reason: Scope-backed: the PRD's outOfScope names this exact case as explicitly not pinned ('US-003 only: whether Exec (RunCommand with argv) admits a positional ./.nax/config.json under a clean scan is not pinned'). The observed behaviour is the read gate's own semantics propagated, not a bypass: normalizeExec's positional screen consults the injected configRefusal, which is open only under the same configReadable predicate (clean scan AND raw-or-absent Bash) that governs Read/Grep/Glob, so a gated dispatch or any finding keeps the refusal (pinned by the moved test at coding-tool-support-owned-paths.test.ts:170-187). A clean scan means the scanner found nothing in exactly the path set the gate can admit, so no secret is disclosed, and package-manager install verbs treat the positional token as a source — they never write the named file, so .nax/config.json cannot be modified from this branch with or without the OS sandbox.

rationale: Verified in code: resolveWithin is the only screen findPositionalPathConflict uses (package-managers.ts:355-362, policy-paths-branch.ts:102-110), and Exec's argvBranch (policy.ts:191-235) short-circuits before applyPathRules, so writeRefusal is indeed not consulted there — but the branch is gated by the same configReadable the rest of the gate uses (coding-tool-support-resolve.ts:515-546). The residual is a read-tool-equivalent, self-consistent consequence the PRD deliberately left unpinned, and its residual safety (no write to the config; nothing to disclose when the scan is clean) holds. Waiving keeps the spec intact; a blanket Exec refusal would contradict the clean-opens-reads design, and adding an AC would mean superseding a spec line that is still accurate enough to stand.
